text: The Baz-Valle systematic review concluded that 12-20 weekly sets per muscle group may be an optimum standard for muscle growth in young, trained men.

cite.quote: a range of 12-20 weekly sets per muscle group may be an optimum standard recommendation for increasing muscle hypertrophy in young, trained men

text: In the Baz-Valle systematic review, no significant difference was found between moderate and high training volume for the quadriceps (p = 0.19) or the biceps brachii (p = 0.59).

cite.quote: there were no differences between moderate and high training volume responses for the quadriceps (p = 0.19) and the biceps brachii (p = 0.59)

text: The Baz-Valle systematic review concluded that a high training volume appears to be better for muscle mass gains in the triceps brachii (p = 0.01).

cite.quote: a high training volume is better to induce muscle mass gains in the triceps brachii (p = 0.01)

text: The Schoenfeld review found a graded dose-response relationship: increases in resistance training volume produced greater gains in muscle hypertrophy.

cite.quote: The findings indicate a graded dose-response relationship whereby increases in RT volume produce greater gains in muscle hypertrophy.

text: The Schoenfeld review's abstract concludes that, comparing studies on a volume-equated basis, training twice a week promotes superior hypertrophic outcomes to once a week.

cite.quote: on a volume-equated basis, the current body of evidence indicates that frequencies of training twice a week promote superior hypertrophic outcomes to once a week

text: One study concluded that hamstrings muscle size can be increased more effectively by seated than by prone (lying) leg curl training.

cite.quote: Hamstrings muscle size can be more effectively increased by seated than prone leg curl training

text: One study concluded that standing calf raises were by far more effective than seated calf raises for growing the gastrocnemius, and recommended them.

cite.quote: Standing calf-raise was by far more effective, therefore recommended, than seated calf-raise for inducing muscle hypertrophy of the gastrocnemius

text: In the Kinoshita calf-raise study, soleus growth was similar between the two legs (2.1% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.410).
